Performance Shock Test Systems
17 Mandeville Court, Monterey, California 93940 | 831.655.6600 | lansmont.com
Test Equipment | Instruments | Support Services
Mechanical shock tests accurately measure the fragility of products and evaluate how they respond to particular shock inputs. Shock test data is key information to ensure any product is capable of withstanding its intended “real world” use. To make shock testing as simple and easy as possible, each Performance Shock System is outfitted standard with TouchTest™ Shock II Controls which communicate seamlessly with Test Partner Data Acquisition Systems.
Lansmont Performance Shock Test Systems are intended for testing applications that require testing capabilities above that which we can achieve with our standard shock systems. To provide the increased testing capability, Performance Shock Systems feature optional acceleration systems, suspended seismic reaction masses, and heavier load frames. Shock Test Systems TouchTest Shock 2 Controls TouchTest Shock 2 is designed specifically with test efficiency and ease of use in mind. From a small, high-resolution LCD touch screen, the user can perform the initial setup and test initiation quickly and easily. Simple touch screen menus enable the user to make convenient adjustments to machine settings and to provide total control of the Lansmont Shock Test System during operation. TouchTest Shock 2 Features
• One-button operation to reduce test cycle time • Auto cycle control mode, allowing drop cycles up to 32,000 drops • hock pulse estimator... Open the catalog to page 3
Shock Test Systems FEATURES
Guide Rods When moving the shock table structure up or down prior to a shock test or when the table falls during the shock pulse event, it travels on solid steel, chrome-plated Guide Rods. The Guide Rods are machined to tight tolerances to maintain precise alignment between the table and shock pulse programming during impact. The Guide Rods are also the surfaces that the shock table brake pistons act against following the shock event to avoid any secondary impacts. Shock Test Systems OPTIONS
Table Structure Table design greatly influences the performance of your shock system. Lansmont designs tables as light as possible for maximum performance with enough stiffness such that the table’s frequency response does not adversely affect shock pulse quality. Performance shock system tables vary in size from 9 in. (23 cm) square up to 48 in. (122 cm). Shock Pulse Programmers The table structure impacts a shock pulse programmer during a shock test to create the waveform needed for the testing application.
